_meta.name: lexical_entity_v1
_meta.purpose: Complementary eval set to eval_dataset.json. Where the original set paraphrases titles into natural-language questions (favouring bi-encoder semantic matching), this set targets EXACT lexical signals: named systems, acronyms, compound multi-topic constraints, and numeric identifiers. IR literature holds that sparse retrieval (BM25) outperforms dense on rare-token and entity queries, because embeddings smooth over infrequent tokens while term matching does not.
_meta.hypothesis: hybrid (FAISS + BM25) > dense-only on this set, reversing the ordering observed on eval_dataset.json.
_meta.honest_caveat: This set was deliberately constructed in a style expected to favour lexical retrieval. It is NOT a neutral benchmark and must be reported alongside eval_dataset.json, never in place of it. The pair together characterise where each strategy wins; either alone is misleading.
_meta.id_format: Bare arXiv ID, no URL prefix, no version suffix. evaluate.py normalizes both sides.
question_styles: named_system: query contains the paper's distinctive system/method name
compound: query constrains on two topics that must both be satisfied
numeric: query contains a number, version, or size that appears in the title
rare_token: query hinges on one low-frequency technical term
